text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
- The Finance Ministry plans to annul all special registration papers for passanger cars that have been turned into vans, to make their owners pay higher taxes.

- The Industry Ministry does not want Universal to assemble Hundai cars, saying it is not beneficial for the Polish industry. South Korea's Daewoo, which plans to invest heavily in Poland, is protesting against the Hundai assembly.
- The government starts selling on Wednesday part of its diesel fuel reserves to stabilise the market. It plans to sell about 120,000 tonnes of diesel fuel.
- Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimorzewicz appointed temporary heads of ministries to be created under the government's economic ministries reorganisation.
- The president of the National Bank of Poland said interest rates were relativlely low and that a rate move was unlikely in the near term.
- The goverment said it would hold the first tender to sell diesel fuel from Poland's state reserves on September 18. It ruled out duty-free fuel imports in near term.

- The Polish Peasant Party, the smaller group in the ruling coalition, refused to meet the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) for talks on the planned cabinet reshuffle. The Peasants failed to show up at the coalition meeting late on Tuesday because SLD's Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz allegedly did not consult them over recent appointments.
Poland will sign a 25-year contract with Russia on natural gas delivery on September 25, the industry minister said.
- Poland's largest tractor maker, state-owned Ursus, has problems with sales and its employees work only three days a week.
